findings.question: Can an acoustic-only estimator distinguish two models related by a latent change of coordinates?
findings.control: positive control (shared-alpha world): rejects on 100% of replicates, median statistic 0.285 vs null 95th pct 0.148 -- the same test separates worlds that genuinely differ
findings.notes: the twin rejects on 20% of replicates and the same-world calibrator on 0%, both at the nominal 5% level. The two worlds are not merely hard to tell apart; they are the same distribution. Any estimator that reports 'the' latent coordinates is reporting its own initialisation. Note also that the transition-*blind* version of this test has no power at all against the positive control (p = 0.88): conditioning on the transition is what makes the comparison informative.
findings.error_label: max absolute difference of the clean acoustics

findings.question: Are the latent coordinates themselves recoverable?
findings.control: the affine reparameterisation residual, which is the same quantity modulo h
findings.notes: the two latents differ by 42% and agree to 5.74e-02 once an affine map is allowed. The recoverable object is the equivalence class (Phi, F) / coordinate changes -- Hypothesis 2, measured.
findings.error_label: relative gap between the two latents

findings.question: What IS invariant -- do the two models share a recoverable quantity?
findings.control: the state matrices themselves differ by 9%
findings.notes: a change of latent basis conjugates the state matrix, and conjugation preserves the spectrum. So the poles are the right thing to report, and A_u is not -- two estimators disagreeing about A_u may be describing exactly the same dynamics.
findings.error_label: relative difference between the two recovered pole sets
